Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

strofreal

Format a number as zero-padded text

Stata 

generate z = strofreal(x, "%06.0f")

R base 

data$z <- sprintf('%06.0f',data$x)

Stata reference · R reference

strpos

Whether a string contains some text

Stata 

generate has = strpos(name, "a") > 0

R stringr 

mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, fixed("a")))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Locate a literal ASCII substring with zero for absence

Stata 

generate z = strpos(s, "cat")

R base 

position <- regexpr('cat',data$s,fixed=TRUE); data$z <- ifelse(position<0,0L,as.integer(position))

Stata reference · R reference

strproper

Title case

Stata 

generate s = strproper(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_to_title(name))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Capitalize words in English place names

Stata 

generate z = strproper(s)

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_to_title(data$s,locale='en')

Differs from Stata English locale example; punctuation and language-specific capitalization can differ.

Stata reference · R reference

strreverse

Reverse plain ASCII text

Stata 

generate z = strreverse(s)

R base 

data$z <- vapply(strsplit(data$s,''),function(z) paste(rev(z),collapse=''),character(1))

Stata reference · R reference

strrtrim

Trim trailing ASCII spaces only

Stata 

generate z = strrtrim(s)

R base 

data$z <- sub(' +$','',data$s)

Stata reference · R reference

strtoname

Turn text into a valid name

Stata 

generate n = strtoname(s)

R base 

mutate(data, n = make.names(s))

Differs from Stata janitor::clean_names(data) cleans every variable name at once. make.names() allows dots and follows R reserved-word rules; strtoname() follows Stata allowed-character and length limits.

Stata reference · R reference

Convert short ASCII text to Stata-style names

Stata 

generate z = strtoname(s)

R base 

data$z <- substr(gsub('[^A-Za-z0-9_]','_',data$s),1,32); data$z <- ifelse(grepl('^[0-9]',data$z),paste0('_',data$z),data$z)

Differs from Stata Demonstrated short ASCII names only; R syntactic names and Stata reserved names follow different rules.

Stata reference · R reference

strtrim

Remove leading and trailing spaces

Stata 

generate s = strtrim(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_trim(name))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Trim leading and trailing ASCII spaces

Stata 

generate z = strtrim(s)

R base 

data$z <- trimws(data$s,whitespace=' ')

Stata reference · R reference

strupper

Upper case

Stata 

generate s = strupper(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_to_upper(name))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Uppercase ASCII text

Stata 

generate z = strupper(s)

R base 

data$z <- toupper(data$s)

Stata reference · R reference

subinstr

Replace text

Stata 

generate s = subinstr(name, "a", "b", .)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_replace_all(name, fixed("a"), "b"))

Differs from Stata stringr treats patterns as regular expressions; fixed() matches the text literally, as subinstr() does. R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Replace every literal occurrence

Stata 

generate z = subinstr(s, "cat", "dog", .)

R base 

data$z <- gsub('cat','dog',data$s,fixed=TRUE)

Stata reference · R reference

Replace only the first literal occurrence

Stata 

generate z = subinstr(s, "cat", "dog", 1)

R base 

data$z <- sub('cat','dog',data$s,fixed=TRUE)

Stata reference · R reference

subinword

Replace a complete word in simple ASCII text

Stata 

generate z = subinword(s, "cat", "dog", .)

R base 

data$z <- gsub('\\bcat\\b','dog',data$s,perl=TRUE)

Differs from Stata Uses regular-expression word boundaries; delimiters and Unicode rules can differ from Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

substr

Part of a string

Stata 

generate s = substr(name, 1, 3)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_sub(name, 1, 3))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Extract the last three ASCII characters

Stata 

generate z = substr(s, -3, .)

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_sub(data$s,-3)

Stata reference · R reference

Extract an ASCII prefix by length

Stata 

generate z = substr(s, 1, 3)

R stringr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = stringr::str_sub(s, 1, 3))

Stata reference · R reference

Extract ASCII text using start and length

Stata 

generate z = substr(s, 3, 2)

R stringr 

data <- dplyr::mutate(data, z = stringr::str_sub(s, 3, 4))

Stata reference · R reference

2 more examples and alternatives

Extract an ASCII prefix by length

Stata 

generate z = substr(s, 1, 3)

R base 

data$z <- substr(data$s,1,3)

Stata reference · R reference

Extract ASCII text using start and length

Stata 

generate z = substr(s, 3, 2)

R base 

data$z <- substr(data$s,3,4)

Stata takes a length; base R substr takes an inclusive ending position.

Stata reference · R reference

uchar

Create characters from Unicode code points

Stata 

generate z = uchar(code)

R base 

data$z <- vapply(data$code,intToUtf8,character(1))

Stata reference · R reference

upper

Upper case

Stata 

generate s = upper(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, s = str_to_upper(name))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

ustrlen

Count Unicode code points

Stata 

generate z = ustrlen(s)

R base 

data$z <- nchar(data$s,type='chars')

Counts code points, not visible grapheme clusters.

Stata reference · R reference

ustrlower

Lowercase Unicode text with an explicit locale

Stata 

generate z = ustrlower(s)

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_to_lower(data$s,locale='en')

Differs from Stata The locale is explicitly English; choose the relevant locale for language-sensitive casing.

Stata reference · R reference

ustrnormalize

Normalize canonically equivalent Unicode text

Stata 

generate z = ustrnormalize(s, "nfc")

R stringi 

data$z <- stringi::stri_trans_nfc(data$s)

Stata reference · R reference

Normalize compatibility Unicode characters

Stata 

generate z = ustrnormalize(s, "nfkc")

R stringi 

data$z <- stringi::stri_trans_nfkc(data$s)

Stata reference · R reference

ustrpos

Locate a Unicode substring by code-point position

Stata 

generate z = ustrpos(s, "猫")

R base 

position <- regexpr('\u732b',data$s,fixed=TRUE); data$z <- ifelse(position<0,0L,as.integer(position))

Stata reference · R reference

ustrregexm

Unicode-aware regular expression, ignoring case

Stata 

generate has = ustrregexm(name, "^a", 1)

R stringr 

mutate(data, has = str_detect(name, regex("^a", ignore_case = TRUE)))

Differs from Stata stringr is Unicode-aware throughout, so the u- forms of Stata's string functions need no special version. R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Detect Unicode letters

Stata 

generate z = ustrregexm(s, "\p{L}+")

R stringr 

data$z <- as.integer(stringr::str_detect(data$s,'\\p{L}+'))

Differs from Stata ICU regex workflow; missing strings in R remain NA rather than empty Stata strings.

Stata reference · R reference

ustrregexra

Replace every ICU regex match

Stata 

generate z = ustrregexra(s, "[0-9]+", "#")

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_replace_all(data$s,'[0-9]+','#')

Stata reference · R reference

ustrregexrf

Replace the first ICU regex match

Stata 

generate z = ustrregexrf(s, "[0-9]+", "#")

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_replace(data$s,'[0-9]+','#')

Stata reference · R reference

ustrreverse

Reverse Unicode code-point order

Stata 

generate z = ustrreverse(s)

R stringi 

data$z <- stringi::stri_reverse(data$s)

Differs from Stata Combining marks and grapheme clusters may require a different user-facing reversal rule.

Stata reference · R reference

ustrtrim

Trim Unicode whitespace

Stata 

generate z = ustrtrim(s)

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_trim(data$s)

Stata reference · R reference

ustrupper

Uppercase Unicode text with an explicit locale

Stata 

generate z = ustrupper(s)

R stringr 

data$z <- stringr::str_to_upper(data$s,locale='en')

Differs from Stata Explicit English locale; locale-specific casing can differ from Stata defaults.

Stata reference · R reference

usubstr

Extract one Unicode code point by position

Stata 

generate z = usubstr(s, 2, 1)

R base 

data$z <- substr(data$s,2,2)

R character indexing follows code points; this does not count grapheme clusters.

Stata reference · R reference

word

The first word of a string

Stata 

generate w = word(name, 1)

R stringr 

mutate(data, w = stringr::word(name, 1))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Extract the second simple whitespace word

Stata 

generate z = word(s, 2)

R base 

data$z <- vapply(strsplit(trimws(data$s),' +'),function(z) z[2],character(1))

Differs from Stata Simple unquoted words with at least two tokens; Stata quoted-word parsing is not reproduced.

Stata reference · R reference

wordcount

Number of words

Stata 

generate n = wordcount(name)

R stringr 

mutate(data, n = str_count(name, "\\S+"))

Differs from Stata R Unicode, regular-expression and case rules can differ from non-ustr Stata string functions; Stata empty strings are missing whereas R distinguishes empty strings and NA.

Stata reference · R reference

Count simple whitespace-separated words

Stata 

generate z = wordcount(s)

R base 

data$z <- ifelse(trimws(data$s)=='',0L,lengths(strsplit(trimws(data$s),' +')))

Differs from Stata Unquoted ASCII words only; quoted multiword phrases need a parser.

Stata reference · R reference

year

Year of a date

Stata 

generate y = year(d)

R lubridate 

mutate(data, y = lubridate::year(d))

lubridate::month(), day() and wday() extract the other parts.

Stata reference · R reference

Extract calendar years

Stata 

generate z = year(d)

R base 

data$z <- as.integer(format(data$d,'%Y'))

Differs from Stata Accepts an R Date column and returns the demonstrated calendar component; raw Stata date codes require conversion first.

Stata reference · R reference

ym

Construct Stata monthly codes from year and month

Stata 

generate z = ym(year, month)

R base 

data$z <- (data$year-1960L)*12L+data$month-1L

Differs from Stata Requires valid integer months 1–12; output uses Stata months since January 1960.

Stata reference · R reference

yq

Construct Stata quarterly codes from year and quarter

Stata 

generate z = yq(year, quarter)

R base 

data$z <- (data$year-1960L)*4L+data$quarter-1L

Differs from Stata Requires valid integer quarters 1–4; output uses quarters since 1960q1.
